page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8y.16xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the ARM architecture. The instance is powered by the custom Alibaba Yitian YiTian710 processor running at 2.75 GHz, providing 64 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading. It is provisioned with 256 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, alongside 64 MB of shared L3 cache and dedicated hardware AES acceleration. Networking throughput is provisioned with a 32 Gbps baseline bandwidth. The instance features no bundled local storage and includes zero GPUs, requiring persistent data to be attached via network storage volumes.

Benchmark results highlight strong multi-core scalability and memory subsystem performance. In stress-ng multi-core testing and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, the 64-core Yitian processor reaches the top 25 percent tier, whereas single-core testing demonstrates average execution speeds. PassMark memory testing registers in the top 10 percent, supported by strong cached read memory bandwidth. In-memory data workloads exhibit high throughput, reflected by 93.0 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and strong database operation scores.

From an architectural standpoint, the single-thread-per-core design eliminates resource contention between hardware threads, improving execution consistency across large concurrent tasks. The lack of bundled local NVMe storage requires architects to evaluate external storage latency and bandwidth costs. ecs.g8y.16xlarge provides high resource density per core, making it an efficient choice for memory-bound caching layers, containerized microservices, distributed data processing, and enterprise web applications targeting the ARM64 ecosystem.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8y.16xlarge is a general-purpose ARM-based instance driven by a 64-core Alibaba Yitian YiTian710 processor operating at 2.75 GHz. Utilizing a dedicated 1:1 physical-to-virtual core allocation without hyperthreading, the instance provides 256 GB of RAM, a 64 MB L3 cache, and 32 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. It contains no onboard local storage and no GPU accelerators. Performance testing demonstrates top-tier memory scores in PassMark and strong multi-core computational throughput, backed by high cached memory bandwidth and 93.0 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations. Single-thread execution and unbundled disk architecture present clear engineering tradeoffs, making the instance primarily suited for multi-threaded microservices, Redis caching tiers, relational and in-memory databases, and container clusters optimized for 64-bit ARM architectures.
